faq.q: What is the difference between 22K and 24K gold?
faq.a: 24K is 99.9% pure gold (999) - soft, used for coins and bars. 22K is 91.6% gold (916) with 8.4% other metals that make it strong enough for jewellery. Jewellery is almost always 22K or 18K; 24K is the choice for coins and investment.

faq.q: What are making charges?
faq.a: The jeweller's fee for crafting the piece, on top of the gold. It is quoted as a % of the gold value or per gram and varies a lot by jeweller and design - often 8% to 25% for plain gold, higher for intricate work. It is usually the most negotiable part of the bill.

faq.q: How much GST is there on gold jewellery?
faq.a: 3% GST on the value of the gold plus making charges. The rates on MyGoldRates are before GST, so add 3% for the billed price.

faq.q: What is BIS hallmarking and HUID?
faq.a: Every piece of gold jewellery sold in India must carry a BIS hallmark: the BIS logo, the purity (e.g. 22K916) and a 6-character HUID code unique to that piece. You can check the HUID in the government's BIS CARE app.

faq.q: How many grams is one tola?
faq.a: 1 tola = 11.664 grams. In South India a sovereign (pavan) is 8 grams. Ask me the price of any weight, for example "price of 1 tola 22K".

faq.q: Why do jewellers charge different gold rates?
faq.a: Each jeweller sets its own daily rate from the bullion price plus its own premium, so the same 22K can differ by a few hundred rupees per 10 g. That's why we compare them side by side every day.

faq.q: Where do these rates come from?
faq.a: From each jeweller's own published rate, checked against the market: a rate more than 4% away from the other jewellers' is held back as a probable error, not shown. Rates are per gram, before GST.

faq.q: What does 0% deduction on old gold exchange mean?
faq.a: You get the full value of your old gold at today's rate after a purity test, with nothing deducted. Often it applies only to jewellery bought from that same jeweller, and selling for cash usually gets less than exchanging for new jewellery.

faq.q: Is now a good time to buy gold?
faq.a: Nobody can reliably predict tomorrow's gold price, and we don't try. What helps: compare jewellers (the gap is often several thousand rupees on 10 g), watch the recent trend, and set a price alert for the rate you want - we'll email you when it gets there.

faq.q: How do I get daily gold rate alerts?
faq.a: Subscribe free with your email: every morning you get the cheapest jeweller and the market rate, and you can ask to be emailed the day 22K drops to your price.

faq.q: Is 20% off making charges a good deal?
faq.a: Only if the making charge left after the discount is lower than at other jewellers. 20% off an 18% making charge leaves 14.4% - still dearer than a jeweller charging 12% with no offer. The discount never applies to the gold itself. Compare the final price, not the size of the discount.

faq.q: Is 18K gold good for jewellery?
faq.a: 18K is 75% gold. It is harder than 22K, holds stones securely, and costs about 18% less per gram - the usual choice for diamond and lightweight daily-wear jewellery.

faq.q: Should I buy gold coins or jewellery?
faq.a: For investment, 24K coins or bars: low making charges and easier resale. Jewellery carries making charges you don't get back when you sell. Bank coins often cost more than jewellers' coins - compare the per-gram price.

faq.q: How can I check gold purity at home?
faq.a: There is no reliable home test - magnet, biting or vinegar tricks cannot tell 22K from 18K. Check the BIS hallmark and verify its 6-character HUID in the BIS CARE app, or ask for a karatmeter (XRF) test at a jeweller.

faq.q: What is digital gold and is it safe?
faq.a: Digital gold lets you buy small amounts of 24K gold online, held in a vault by the seller's partner. It is not regulated by RBI or SEBI, buying and selling prices differ by a few percent, and 3% GST applies when you buy. Gold ETFs and gold mutual funds are the regulated alternative.

faq.q: Should I buy a gold ETF or physical gold?
faq.a: Gold ETFs and gold mutual funds follow the gold price, are regulated by SEBI, have no making charges or storage worries and can be sold on any working day (ETFs need a demat account). Buy physical gold when you want to wear it; for pure investment, ETFs or 24K coins cost less.

faq.q: What are Sovereign Gold Bonds?
faq.a: Government gold bonds issued through the RBI: they paid 2.5% interest a year plus the gold price at maturity, tax-free if held to maturity. No new bonds have been issued since early 2024; existing ones can be bought and sold on the stock exchange.

faq.q: How much gold can I keep at home?
faq.a: There is no legal limit if you can show where the gold came from. In income-tax searches, officers do not seize up to 500 g for a married woman, 250 g for an unmarried woman and 100 g for a man, even without proof of purchase.

faq.q: How much gold can I bring from Dubai or abroad?
faq.a: Travellers returning to India get a duty-free allowance for gold jewellery that depends on who is travelling and how long they stayed abroad; above it, customs duty is due, and bars and coins are dutiable. Check the current rules on the CBIC (Indian Customs) website before you fly.

faq.q: Is gold cheaper in Dubai?
faq.a: Often a little, because the UAE has no import duty. But gold brought into India above your duty-free allowance pays Indian customs duty, which usually wipes out the saving - compare the final cost including duty, and the making charges, before you buy.

faq.q: What is the hallmarking charge?
faq.a: BIS charges jewellers a small fee per piece for hallmarking - tens of rupees, not hundreds. Some bills show it separately; it should never be a large amount.

faq.q: How much will I get for my old gold?
faq.a: Old gold is valued by weight times purity (tested at the counter) at the jeweller's buying rate, which is usually a little below its selling rate; making charges and stones are not paid back. Exchanging it for new jewellery usually gets more than selling it for cash.

faq.q: What is 916 gold?
faq.a: 916 means 91.6% pure gold - the same as 22K. On the hallmark it appears as 22K916.

faq.q: What is KDM gold?
faq.a: KDM was a cadmium-based solder once used to join gold; it is no longer used because cadmium is harmful. Today '916 KDM' simply means 22K - what matters is the BIS hallmark with its HUID.

faq.q: What is rose gold or white gold?
faq.a: Rose gold is gold mixed with more copper, giving it a pink colour; white gold is gold mixed with white metals and usually rhodium-plated. Both are usually 18K or 14K and priced on their gold content.

faq.q: Is 14K gold real gold?
faq.a: Yes - 14K is 58.5% gold (585). It is harder and cheaper than 18K or 22K, and must still carry a BIS hallmark (14K585).

faq.q: What is 1 gram gold jewellery?
faq.a: '1 gram gold' jewellery is gold-plated or gold-covered imitation jewellery with very little gold in it. It is not hallmarked and has almost no resale value.

faq.q: How much gold loan can I get?
faq.a: Banks and gold-loan companies lend a share of your gold's value, capped by RBI rules, and interest rates vary a lot between lenders - compare a few. Our gold loan calculator estimates how much you could borrow.

faq.q: Why does the gold price go up and down?
faq.a: Indian gold rates follow the international gold price in dollars and the rupee-dollar rate, plus import duty and each jeweller's premium. World events, interest rates and festive demand move them every day.

faq.q: What is the best day to buy gold?
faq.a: No day of the week is reliably cheaper. Festivals like Dhanteras and Akshaya Tritiya bring offers, but also crowds and firmer rates. On whatever day you choose, compare jewellers and today's offers - the gap between them is bigger than day-to-day moves.

faq.q: What about diamond prices?
faq.a: I cover gold only. Diamond prices depend on cut, colour, clarity and carat and are not comparable shop to shop. For the gold in diamond jewellery (usually 18K), ask me the 18K rate.

faq.q: Is this jeweller's gold pure and trustworthy?
faq.a: Every jeweller here must sell BIS-hallmarked jewellery, so purity is checked the same way at all of them: look for the hallmark and verify the HUID in the BIS CARE app. We compare their rates, making charges and offers - not their service.

faq.q: How often are the rates updated?
faq.a: Every morning, after jewellers publish their day's rate. Some jewellers change their rate during the day, so confirm it at the store before you pay.

faq.q: Are the rates including GST?
faq.a: No - all rates here are before GST. Add 3% GST on the gold and making charges for the billed price.

faq.q: How is the price of gold jewellery calculated?
faq.a: Price = weight x today's rate for the karat + making charges (+ stones, if any) + 3% GST on the total. Ask me, for example, "price of 10 g 22K at Tanishq" for a worked bill.

faq.q: Can I return gold jewellery?
faq.a: Return and buyback rules are each jeweller's own - many offer exchange or buyback with a deduction rather than a refund. Ask for the policy in writing on the bill before you pay.

faq.q: How do gold savings schemes work?
faq.a: You pay the jeweller a fixed amount every month for about 10-11 months, and it adds a bonus or waives part of the making charges when you buy jewellery at the end. You can redeem it only as jewellery at that jeweller, and it is not a bank deposit.

faq.q: Can I buy gold on EMI?
faq.a: Usually not: RBI rules stop banks lending to buy gold, and most cards exclude jewellery from EMI. Jewellers' monthly savings schemes are the usual way to pay in instalments.

faq.q: Is PAN needed to buy gold, and is there a cash limit?
faq.a: PAN is needed for a purchase of Rs 2 lakh or more, and a jeweller may not take Rs 2 lakh or more in cash for one purchase. Paying by card, UPI or bank transfer avoids both problems.

faq.q: How is tax charged when I sell gold?
faq.a: Physical gold held more than 24 months: long-term capital gains taxed at 12.5% without indexation. Held less: the gain is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate. Budgets change these rules, so check with a tax adviser.

faq.q: What is the import duty on gold?
faq.a: India imports most of its gold, and the import duty set in the Union Budget is part of every rate you see here; 3% GST is then added on the bill.

faq.q: How do I contact MyGoldRates?
faq.a: Write to us from the Contact page - we read every message, and suggestions for Sona are welcome.

faq.q: Who runs MyGoldRates?
faq.a: MyGoldRates is an independent site that compares the rates, making charges and offers jewellers publish. It is not owned by any jeweller and is free to use.

faq.q: Is this website free?
faq.a: Yes - completely free, with no sign-up needed. The daily rate email is free too.

faq.q: Do you sell gold?
faq.a: No - we don't sell gold. We compare jewellers' rates, making charges and offers so you can buy wherever it works out cheapest; each jeweller's page links to its own website.

faq.q: How do I unsubscribe from the emails?
faq.a: Every email has an Unsubscribe link at the bottom - one tap and you are off the list.

faq.q: How much does a mangalsutra or chain weigh?
faq.a: It varies a lot: a light daily-wear chain or mangalsutra can be 4-8 g, a traditional one 20 g or more. Tell me the weight and I'll work out today's price, e.g. "price of 8 g 22K".

faq.q: What is a pavan?
faq.a: A pavan (or sovereign) is 8 grams of gold, the usual unit in Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Ask me "price of 1 pavan 22K" for today's price.

faq.q: What is the difference between carat and karat?
faq.a: Karat (K) is gold purity: 24K is pure, 22K is 91.6%, 18K is 75%. Carat (ct) is the weight unit for diamonds and gems (1 ct = 0.2 g). In India the two words are often used for both.
